subject: Materials Science
title: Normalizing Steel
description: Learn Normalizing Steel in one minute.

hook.text: Welding leaves behind uneven grain sizes — some coarse, some fine, all unpredictable.

buildup.text: Normalizing heats steel above its critical temperature, then lets it cool in still air.

discovery.text: Air cooling produces uniform fine grains — a reset button for the microstructure.

twist.text: It's faster and cheaper than annealing but gives slightly harder results.

climax.text: Structural steel beams are normalized to guarantee consistent properties across every section.

punchline.text: Normalizing gives steel a fresh, even-grained start.

quiz.question: How does normalizing differ from annealing?
options: Normalizing uses furnace cooling; annealing uses air cooling
Normalizing uses air cooling; annealing uses slower furnace cooling
